The joint indicator conditional expectation equals the product of the two marginal conditional expectations. Finite cylinders require exact equality to the supplied labels on every member of F, and arbitrary measurable schedule events are quantified. Duration bounds multiply the one- or two-gradient job work by tau; completion equality uses the job start plus its duration, not merely an upper deadline.

For every call through eventLimit at the requested batch, every actual before/after pending job has duration<=jobWork*tau. Every active request must receive an actual matching worker/ID and exact jobValue at a finite NNReal completion time c, with c>=current clock and c=start+duration. Every other pending actual finish is at least current clock and at least c; equal finishes are resolved by schedule priority, then worker index. Thus the schedule realizes the actual earliest-completion behavior and retains constraints on final unused dispatches. The finite observation horizon must later be justified by execution progress; this relation contains no expected-time bound or completed-sample law. Before/after batchJobs observations use the accepted PAGE trace and collectorPendingAfter, so old final dispatches are retained without treating the next batch fresh jobs as part of the old one. The priority/worker lexicographic rule determines a unique choice among simultaneous finishes.

Absent/full batches make only the difference factorization inactive, not the schedule-realization obligation for active full batches.
